items.article: Paramount Skydance's David Ellison just introduced new co-CEO Ynon Kreiz ahead of its $110 billion deal with Warner Bros. Discovery. Paramount Skydance's David Ellison just introduced his new co-CEO ahead of the company's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Ynon Kreiz, who'd been the CEO at toy maker Mattel since 2018, is joining Paramount on Monday as it finalizes its $110 billion merger with WBD . "I always planned to partner with an executive of Ynon's caliber. Our skills and experience complement each other, and we share a vision for what this company can become," Ellison told employees in a memo, which was obtained by Business Insider. Paramount said in its announcement that Ellison would lead the combined company's creative and tech strategy, while Kreiz would oversee day-to-day operations and deal integration. Ellison said there's "nobody I'd rather have standing next to me" than Kreiz, whom he called a "proven builder and operator, who shares our vision and cares deeply about our creative mission." Kreiz took steps to turn Mattel into an entertainment company by adapting toys like Barbie and Matchbox into movies. Mattel's Barbie movie, produced by Warner Bros., grossed over $1.4 billion globally in 2023, though this summer's "Masters of the Universe" film, based on the He-Man toys, fell short of expectations. Under Kreiz, Mattel had planned to make more movies.
